questions.subject: accountancy
questions.question: A new partner pays a cash premium for goodwill directly to the existing partners, privately. The firm does not receive or record the payment. What should the firm record in its books for this payment?
questions.body: A new partner pays a cash premium for goodwill directly to the existing partners, privately. The firm does not receive or record the payment. What should the firm record in its books for this payment?

options.text: No journal entry should be passed.
Debit Bank A/c and credit Premium for Goodwill A/c.
Debit Goodwill A/c and credit the sacrificing partners’ capital accounts.
Debit the new partner’s capital account and credit the sacrificing partners’ capital accounts.

questions.subject: accountancy
questions.question: A, B, C and D continue as partners; no partner is admitted or retires. Their old profit-sharing ratio is 5:3:2:2, and their agreed new ratio is 7:5:4:2. The firm has goodwill, and its value is to be adjusted for the change in ratio. Which treatment correctly identifies the sacrificing and gaining partners and records the goodwill adjustment?
questions.body: A, B, C and D continue as partners; no partner is admitted or retires. Their old profit-sharing ratio is 5:3:2:2, and their agreed new ratio is 7:5:4:2. The firm has goodwill, and its value is to be adjusted for the change in ratio. Which treatment correctly identifies the sacrificing and gaining partners and records the goodwill adjustment?

options.text: A and D are sacrificing partners and B and C are gaining partners; credit A and D, and debit B and C.
A and D are gaining partners and B and C are sacrificing partners; debit A and D, and credit B and C.
A, B and C are gaining partners and D is unchanged; debit A, B and C, and leave D unadjusted.
A and D are sacrificing partners and B and C are gaining partners; debit A and D, and credit B and C.

An enterprise is preparing a cash flow statement for an accounting period. Consider the following statements about its presentation.
(A) The statement reports the change in the position of cash and cash equivalents over the accounting period.
(B) Activities contributing to this change are classified as operating, investing and financing activities.
(C) Under each activity heading, it is sufficient to show only the net cash flow (or use), rather than full details of inflows and outflows.
(D) The aggregate net cash flow (or use) is worked out from the net amounts of the operating, investing and financing activities.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.body:

questions.subject: accountancy
questions.question: A firm maintains partners’ accounts under the fixed capital method. During the year, partner R is allocated a share of profit and makes ordinary drawings. No additional capital is introduced, and no part of R’s capital is withdrawn under the partnership agreement. What happens to R’s Capital Account during the year?
questions.body: A firm maintains partners’ accounts under the fixed capital method. During the year, partner R is allocated a share of profit and makes ordinary drawings. No additional capital is introduced, and no part of R’s capital is withdrawn under the partnership agreement. What happens to R’s Capital Account during the year?

options.text: It is increased by the share of profit allocated to R.
It remains unchanged during the year.
It is reduced by the ordinary drawings made by R.
It is adjusted for both the share of profit and the ordinary drawings.

questions.subject: accountancy
questions.question: On 31 October 2025, the last balance sheet of a firm was prepared. A partner, entitled to 1/4 of the firm’s profits, died on 31 March 2026. The firm’s profits for the three preceding years were ₹2,40,000, ₹3,00,000 and ₹3,60,000. For this estimate, the firm uses the average of those three annual profits and assumes profit accrues evenly over the 12-month year. What is the deceased partner’s estimated share of profit for the five-month period from 1 November 2025 to 31 March 2026?
questions.body: On 31 October 2025, the last balance sheet of a firm was prepared. A partner, entitled to 1/4 of the firm’s profits, died on 31 March 2026. For this estimate, the firm uses the average of those three annual profits and assumes profit accrues evenly over the 12-month year. What is the deceased partner’s estimated share of profit for the five-month period from 1 November 2025 to 31 March 2026?

questions.subject: accountancy
questions.question: Leena and Farah agree orally to enter into a partnership. They have not prepared a written document. Which statement correctly describes whether their agreement must be in writing?
questions.body: Leena and Farah agree orally to enter into a partnership. They have not prepared a written document. Which statement correctly describes whether their agreement must be in writing?

options.text: Their partnership cannot come into existence until the oral terms are put in writing.
Their oral agreement is itself a Partnership Deed.
Their oral agreement can establish the partnership; a written document is not compulsory.
Their partnership can come into existence without an agreement if they prepare a written deed later.

questions.subject: accountancy
questions.question: A, B and C continue as partners without any admission or retirement. Their old profit-sharing ratio is 5:3:2, and their new ratio is 4:2:4. The total goodwill of the firm is valued at ₹90,000 and is to be adjusted through the partners’ capital accounts. For this question, the amount transferred for goodwill is the total goodwill multiplied by the fraction of profit transferred. Credit the sacrificing partners in proportion to their sacrifices and debit the gaining partners in proportion to their gains. Which adjustment is correct?
questions.body: A, B and C continue as partners without any admission or retirement. Their old profit-sharing ratio is 5:3:2, and their new ratio is 4:2:4. The total goodwill of the firm is valued at ₹90,000 and is to be adjusted through the partners’ capital accounts. For this question, the amount transferred for goodwill is the total goodwill multiplied by the fraction of profit transferred. Credit the sacrificing partners in proportion to their sacrifices and debit the gaining partners in proportion to their gains. Which adjustment is correct?

options.text: Debit C’s Capital A/c ₹18,000; credit A’s Capital A/c ₹9,000 and B’s Capital A/c ₹9,000.
Debit C’s Capital A/c ₹90,000; credit A’s Capital A/c ₹45,000 and B’s Capital A/c ₹45,000.
Debit C’s Capital A/c ₹18,000; credit A’s Capital A/c ₹11,250 and B’s Capital A/c ₹6,750.
Debit C’s Capital A/c ₹18,000; credit A’s Capital A/c ₹12,000 and B’s Capital A/c ₹6,000.
